notes.1.103: ꜥꜣt taken as a strip or piece; jdmyt is a fine (red?) linen. 'It is untied' (wḥꜥ.tw=f) may refer to the amulet, or to the birth ('he is released'). mnḫ[.w], with its plural ending, is taken as 'strung', of the amulets.
notes.1.109: qmꜣ and ꜥnbw are plants (reeds or rushes?) not certainly identified. qnw=s, 'her bosom' or 'embrace', is uncertain. 'Good, good' (nfr nfr) is repeated in the text.
notes.1.125: The šꜣjwt, Khadjaruti, Shaarutit and the ꜥmꜣmyt of the West are demonesses; ꜥmꜣmyt is perhaps 'swallower'. 'Every great one' (wrt nbt) may instead go with the West ('the great West'); hrr is not understood. In 1.126 'you' is plural.

nodes.text: Words to be spoken over a falcon, a cat, and a wedjat-eye of faience, strung on a strip of *jdmyt*-linen,
given to a woman at her rear; it is untied
and placed at the throat of her son on the day of his birth.
N, born of N, lies on a mat of *qmꜣ*; variant: on a clean mat of *ꜥnbw*.
Ipet the Great makes her protection,
the gods and goddesses guard her.

If that enemy, dead man, dead woman, male or female adversary, sorcery, or any evil, bad thing comes to fall upon N, born of N, in the hour of the day, then the 7 fighters [will be] good, good at driving the adversary away from N, born of N,
each one of them making her protections.

You shall drive away every fear, every terror, every dread of the *šꜣjwt*, Khadjaruti, Shaarutit, the *ꜥmꜣmyt* of the West, every great one(?), every *hrr*, every evil, bad thing that comes to harm N, born of N, by night, by day, at any time.
You shall not let them come to the birth-house.
